why: The hatched sign has a hook with a dot touching it inside the angle. Both l and the dotted t fit, and no entry covers it.
The (5) sign has a flat 3-like top with a straight descender to the lower left. That is ẖ; this hand's k has its long tail to the lower right.
Only one slash stands before the hook at (7); my extra o was a hatching stroke. The crossed group after r begins with a slash and is te, not l i.
The o is uncertain and may be the thick end of the spout outline. r te? y agree with the copy. The last sign is a long slash left of a hook, te, not a dotted t.
The slash left of a barred 4 is te, as in the identical tedḫelowi group after it. The sic 3 is ḫ (Index C tedḫeli, Kar. 81).
The (4) sign is a 3 whose tail curls into a loop at the foot. That is this hand's w, and the small crossed sign after it is i, as in -lowi.
The small sign after atqoli is a single curved stroke. Griffith prints a queried divider there and the other reader reads l?; the copy does not decide.
The slash before the n's 3 is the n's own rising stroke. The two strokes left of it are l (marked sic) and o, giving nlotetelowi as printed in Index B.
The strokes between n and te are the n's stroke, l and o (type nlotetelowi), not a y.
The sign is a hook with no tail of its own; the long line under it is the k's tail. It fits t, as in Griffith's prose t(?)ik, not this hand's long-tailed p.
The last sign before 'end' is hatched with traces. Griffith's formula B table and Index C print it as e (pi(?)ke).
